chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ajlan Abi Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about devouring the wealth of the orphans, so he (peace be upon him) said: It is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: 'Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only devouring into their bellies fire, and they will be burned in a Blaze.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said, without me asking him: 'Whoever shelters an orphan until his orphanhood ceases or he becomes self-sufficient, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated Paradise for him, just as He has obligated the Fire for the one who devours the wealth of the orphan.'

key_terms.أَكْلِ مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: Devouring the wealth of the orphans

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for caring for an orphan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a direct thematic parallel between the grave sin of devouring orphans' wealth and the immense reward of their care, using the Quranic imagery of 'eating fire' to denote internalizing divine punishment. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the moral weight of guardianship (kafalah), framing the support of an orphan not merely as charity but as a guaranteed path to Paradise, mirroring the certainty of Hell for injustice.
